newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi wants loyalty from returning Vietnamese.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi wants loyalty from returning Vietnamese.

text.p: Hanoi has announced new rules for people seeking to return from overseas and re-establish Vietnamese nationality, including a requirement for political loyalty.

Saturday's official Nhan Dan newspaper said the directive -- aimed at the roughly two million Vietnamese overseas -- required a "clear political attitude and non-involvement or support for any organisation seeking to sabotage the Fatherland".

Applications for Vietnamese nationality would also have to be supported by guarantors inside Vietnam and would be refused to people who failed to detail their life-history or the situation which led them to moving abroad, it said.
The new rules were signed into effect on November 21. Nhan Dan did not make clear whether Hanoi would recognise or allow returning citizens to keep passports issued to them by foreign governments.
Many Vietnamese living outside their homeland fled their country following the Vietnam war.

Hanoi has traditionally viewed them with suspicion but in recent years has begun encouraging their return to help in the process of investing in and rebuilding a poverty-stricken and war-shattered economy.
